thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO burn-rate exceeded for service=model-serving-prod. burn-rate=12.3x over 10m. Paging @Alex W. and @Oncall-2. Incident priority: P1.

Alex W.: Saw the page, jumping in. What exact symptoms?

Mina P.: Seeing 5xx spike + tail latency spike on long sequences. Affected route: /v1/generate (prod region us-west-2). Error rate up to ~4.8% for last 12m. Not all customers, but some high-throughput clients hit hard.

Jordan L.: I can pull traces and the tracing shows timeouts on the GPU nodes hitting OOM backpressure around step 8 for longer seqs. Possibly KV cache pressure + increased concurrency.

Alex W.: Ok, immediate plan: (1) scale pool up two nodes (done), (2) temporarily route heavy clients to dedicated fallback model variant (lower context window), (3) mute the noisy burn-rate page while we stabilize and create gated paging criteria.

Oncall-2: scaling started (k8s autoscaler) — new pods coming up. Routing change applied for three biggest customers (traffic-shift rule id: ts-20260315-1). Observed drop in error rate to ~2.1% after routing, but latency still elevated.

Sarah G.: Customer-facing: Product-Ops — can you create an incident banner? We should notify the customers we routed them to a lower-context variant to reduce failures. Small chance of slightly different outputs.

Product-Ops: On it — drafting banner: "We’re experiencing increased latency and errors on text generation. Traffic for some high-volume customers has been routed to a lower-latency model variant; outputs may differ slightly. Working on fixes; ETA ~30-45m."

Mina P.: Quick note on alert noise: the burn-rate page we got is single-window 10m with threshold 10x. That was designed to be sensitive for emerging issues but it paged immediately. We need multi-window correlation to avoid paging for transient spikes.

Alex W.: Agreed. Suggested temporary change: require (burn-rate 10m > 10x) AND (burn-rate 1h > 2.5x) to trigger a page. Also add a 'no-paging' label for spikes caused only by scheduled heavy workloads (we saw a bulk ingest from partner-xyz at 11:02).

Jordan L.: I can implement the two-window condition in the alert rule. Proposed alert snippet:

```
alert: SLOBurnrate_Page
expr: (burnrate_ratio{window="10m"} > 10)
  and (burnrate_ratio{window="1h"} > 2.5)
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
  paging: "true"
annotations:
  summary: "SLO burn-rate high across 10m and 1h windows"
```

Alex W.: Add an additional guard: require error_budget_remaining < 0.75 for the service to page. We don't want to page if the budget is still healthy and spike is transient.

Mina P.: Also propose to lower the 'for' to 3m for the 10m window check to speed detection for real sustained regressions, but keep the 1h window as is. We should document this in runbook then.

Oncall-2: I applied a temporary mute on the original single-window alert (rule id slo-burn-10m) for 40m while we test the new rule. Added a Slack note to #eng-monitoring.

Sarah G.: Post-incident actions:
- Create a dedicated dashboard tile showing burn-rate by window (10m, 30m, 1h), error budget remaining, and top client traffic during the spike.
- Update runbook section "SLO burn-rate paging" with new multi-window policy and exception process for partner-initiated bulk.
- Schedule a postmortem to decide if the long-term policy should change (multi-window AND client-aware paging).

Jordan L.: I'll push the dashboard JSON to Grafana (dash id: ds-2332) and create a saved view for oncall. Also create an alert test harness so we can simulate burn-rate patterns and ensure no false pages.

Alex W.: For immediate mitigation, we should also tune autoscaler thresholds to be more aggressive for this service: decrease target CPU by 10% and increase max pods by 25% for the next 2 hours. I have a PR open: links to PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood-inference/infra/PR-4721

Mina P.: Noting customer impact summary for postmortem: ~5 high-throughput customers experienced ~10-20% request retries and ~2-5% result divergence due to fallback model routing. No data breach. Resolution actions: scaling + routing + temporary alert tuning.

Product-Ops: Banner updated, customers notified via support and status page. No major escalations yet.

Alex W.: Action items and owners:
- Jordan: deploy new alert rule + dashboard (ETA 25m)
- Mina: update runbook with paging criteria + exception flow (ETA 2h)
- Alex: monitor error budget + coordinate rollback of mutes (ETA 40m)
- Sarah/Product-Ops: follow up on customer comms and support tickets (ongoing)

Oncall-2: marking the incident as "stabilized" — error rate down to 0.9% and burn-rate ratio dropping to 1.8x (10m). Will keep monitoring for 1h.

Mina P.: Quick reminder: we also need to add a label to alerts to indicate "caused-by-bulk-ingest" so SRE runbooks can decide not to page. I'll add detection heuristics to the pipeline that flags sudden client-side traffic surges > 200% baseline.

Jordan L.: New alert rule pushed and smoke-tested. Grafana dashboard updated. Links: grafana.internal/d/2332/slo-burnrate-overview.

Alex W.: Removing the temporary mute now, replacing with new multi-window rule in production. Keep this thread for follow-ups. Great work everyone. :clap:

Product-Ops: Filing a short customer impact note and postmortem stub in #postmortems (will ping once created).

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: Stabilized -> Monitoring.

Sarah G.: We'll run the postmortem tomorrow 10:30am PT. Agenda: root cause, alert policy changes, autoscaling policy tuning, client bulk-ingest detection, and customer communication lessons.

Alex W.: End of thread for now. I'll follow up with data in the postmortem doc. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
